name: Sludge drying beds; wastewater treatment unit, cement/concrete industry; at plant
description: This unit process reflects operation of sludge drying beds for U.S. cement and concrete plants. The functional unit reflects sludge management associated with treatment of 1 cubic meter of wastewater from a relevant facility. The scope of this process is limited to operation of sludge drying beds. Use the corresponding wastewater treatment process to reflect the full scope of wastewater treatment impacts.
category: 22: Utilities/2213: Water, Sewage and Other Systems

processDocumentation.timeDescription: LCI data was developed in CAPDETWorks software based on WWTP planning documents from the period of 2015-2018. Updating background electricity and input data should maintain process relevance so long as the target treatment system matches the defined system.
processDocumentation.technologyDescription: Open air sludge drying beds - sand bed with bottom drain. Sludge is loaded and removed via loader.
processDocumentation.modelingConstantsDescription: Inventory data was generated for a small, theoretical wastewater treatment facility using the CAPDETWorks software package (maintained by Hydromantis). Inventory exchange values were scaled to the quantity of sludge generated per m3 of cement wastewater as compared to the municipal wastewater in the cited EPA report. Background data sources have, in some cases, been updated to reflect newer and/or public data sources.
processDocumentation.completenessDescription: Exclusion of mechanical and electrical equipment from the system boundary is the only known missing, non-trivial inventory item. CAPDET works balances mass to model effluent quality and sludge quantity.
processDocumentation.dataSelectionDescription: All outputs of the CAPDET model that could be used to develop LCI data were included in the model.
processDocumentation.dataTreatmentDescription: Outputs of the CAPDET model are reported on an annual (energy, chemicals) or lifetime (infrastructure) basis. Annual quantities are standardized to the functional unit by dividing by the average quantity of wastewater treated per year. For inventory data reported on a lifetime basis, quantities are standardized to the functional unit by amortizing the inventory item over the expected lifespan of the infrastructure component.
processDocumentation.samplingDescription: The scope of this treatment process includes basic infrastructure and operation of digging equipment to move sludge to and from the drying pad.  Infrastructure disposal and electrical and mechanical equipment are outside of the system boundaries.  Uncertainty ranges are provided on all flows based on the range of sludge that was estimated to be produced per m3 of wastewater (0.37-1.8 kg sludge/m3 wastewater).
processDocumentation.useAdvice: This process reflects only the impact of a single wastewater treatment process.  Use one of the corresponding wastewater treatment systems to model the full scope of wastewater treatment impacts.
processDocumentation.intendedApplication: This process is intended to be used as a background process by LCA practitioners, industry and the general public to model wastewater treatment plant construction and operation. This process needs to be used in combination with other wastewater treatment processes, sludge management processes and an effluent release process to model the full scope of wastewater impacts. The inventory should be sufficient to model TRACI 2.1 impact categories.
processDocumentation.projectDescription: Data were prepared by Eastern Research Group (ERG) on behalf of the U.S. EPA under Contract No. 68HERC20D0029, "Life Cycle Considerations and Systems Analyses of Municipal Water Sustainability Assessments: Conceptual Plan of Market-based Approach to Address Nutrient Compliance for Wastewater Plants in Kickapoo River Watershed."
